successors.note: The Statute of Rhuddlan of 1284 abolished the remaining princely titles and territories. Cliopatria's England 1285 shape holds all four corrected cells; its Gwynedd shapes of 1216-1284 hold two of them (the Corwen and Llansilin cells), which the kingdom-of-gwynedd dossier must not claim for the same years.

capitals.name: Castell Dinas Bran (Llangollen)
capitals.note: The page says the royal seat was Castell Dinas Bran and the religious centre Valle Crucis Abbey, without dates; Henry de Lacy took the castle on 10 May 1277. The start year is the state's, not a dated building of the castle. The castle lies in the Llangollen cell, which every corrected shape contains (Cliopatria's own shapes did not).

rulers.name: Madog ap Gruffudd
rulers.note: Accession in 1191; 'reigned until 1236'; allied with Llywelyn ab Iorwerth by 1215.

rulers.name: Gruffydd II ap Madog
rulers.note: The page gives his reign as 1236-1269.

rulers.name: Madog II ap Gruffydd
rulers.note: Submitted in 1277 and died in battle later that year; the realm was then divided between Llywelyn Fychan and Gruffudd Fychan I.

correction.text: Maelor and Yale, the lands Gruffydd Maelor received first

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 1160-1168: 'Powys split in two in 1160 following the death of Prince Madog ap Maredudd', and Gruffydd 'received Maelor and Yale first' before he 'later added Nanheudwy, Cynllaith, Glyndyfrdwy and Mochnant Is Rhaeadr' (paraphrase; no years). Cliopatria has no Fadog shape before 1169, so the core is drawn: two cells (about 506 km2), the Wrexham plain (Maelor) and the Llangollen cell, which holds Yale and Castell Dinas Brân. The first version reused Cliopatria's 1169 shape for these years; that shape does not fit the page (see 1169).

Cliopatria's shape (1,293.7 km2, bbox 3.61 to 2.85 W and 52.79 to 53.26 N, centroid 3.28 W 53.06 N) rasterises to four cells on the gazetteer's grid: two in Flintshire (Mold and Holywell, i.e. Tegeingl), one at Ruthin (Dyffryn Clwyd) and one at Corwen; none holds Wrexham (Maelor) or Llangollen (Dinas Bran). The commotes the page names (Maelor, Yale, Nanheudwy, Cynllaith, Glyndyfrdwy, Mochnant Is Rhaeadr) lie round Wrexham, Llangollen, Corwen and Llansilin, so the first verdict that they 'fit the shape' was wrong; Tegeingl is not among them, and kingdom-of-gwynedd claims the Mold and Holywell cells for 1169-1210 and from 1212. Corrected to three cells (about 759 km2, 59 per cent of Cliopatria's area): Maelor (Wrexham cell), Yale and Nanheudwy (Llangollen cell, with the castle) and Glyndyfrdwy to Corwen. Left out: the Ruthin cell, which is mostly Dyffryn Clwyd, a district the page does not name (Llanarmon-yn-Iâl, in Yale, falls in it), and the Chirk cell, whose centre is Oswestry. The page gives no area, so there is no infobox comparison. The Corwen cell is the only one of the three that Cliopatria's shape shares; its Powys row held it to 1168.

Corrected to four cells (about 1,012 km2, 81 per cent of Cliopatria's area): the 1169 correction plus the Llansilin cell. No page dates the addition: the Powys Fadog page says Gruffydd 'later added Nanheudwy, Cynllaith, Glyndyfrdwy and Mochnant Is Rhaeadr'; the Madog ap Gruffydd Maelor page has him 'sole ruler of Powys north of the River Rhaeadr' after his brother's death in 1197 and in King John's pay in 1212, and the Llywelyn the Great page does not mention Madog (ledger 1210, confidence 1).

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 1216-1284: Cliopatria ends the row in 1215 and its Gwynedd shape of 1216 contains the Corwen and Llansilin cells (England's 1285 shape contains all four), but the page has the principality continuing under Madog ap Gruffudd (to 1236), Gruffydd II (1236-1269) and Madog II (to 1277), with Dinas Bran dismantled in 1277 and 'the final campaign of Llywelyn ap Gruffudd' in 1282; it ends with the Statute of Rhuddlan in 1284. The relation to Gwynedd: an 'alliance' by 1215, 'forced into an alliance' in 1258, and under the Llywelyn ap Gruffudd page 'All of the Welsh princes submitted to Llywelyn II' in 1267 (Fadog not named): drawn as a vassal tint 1258-1277 (ledger, confidence 1), then English overlordship 1277-1284.

region.text: Maelor and Yale, the lands Gruffydd Maelor received first

ledger.note: 1160: Madog ap Maredudd dies and Powys splits; the northern half becomes Powys Fadog. 'Powys split in two in 1160 following the death of Prince Madog ap Maredudd.' The page has Gruffydd receiving Maelor and Yale first, which is the core drawn here (the Wrexham and Llangollen cells); the other commotes are 'later added'. The page gives the split, not a boundary.

region.text: Glyndyfrdwy, the Dee valley up to Corwen

ledger.note: 1169: Glyndyfrdwy joins the realm in Cliopatria's first Fadog shape. The page says only that Gruffydd 'later added Nanheudwy, Cynllaith, Glyndyfrdwy and Mochnant Is Rhaeadr', without years; the year is that of Cliopatria's first shape, whose Corwen cell its Powys row held to 1168 (Nanheudwy is already in the Llangollen cell). Confidence 1: the page is silent on the date.
1191: the northern realm becomes known as Powys Fadog under Madog ap Gruffudd. 'This northern realm became known as Powys Fadog after the accession in 1191 of his son prince Madog ap Gruffudd.'

region.text: Cynllaith and Mochnant Is Rhaeadr, round Llansilin and Llangedwyn

ledger.note: 1210: Cynllaith and Mochnant Is Rhaeadr are in the realm in Cliopatria's 1210 shape, which adds the Llansilin cell that its Powys Wenwynwyn shape held to 1209. The page gives no year for the addition (see 1169). The Madog ap Gruffydd Maelor page has Madog 'sole ruler of Powys north of the River Rhaeadr' after his brother's death in 1197 (the page's year; the lands are not named) and, in 1212, looking 'to King John of England, in whose pay he was'. The year is Cliopatria's: confidence 1.

ledger.note: 1258: Gruffydd II is forced into Llywelyn ap Gruffudd's alliance. 'In 1258 he was forced into an alliance with prince Llywelyn ap Gruffudd'; 'Llywelyn was recognised as Prince of Wales under the terms of the 1267 Treaty of Montgomery'. The pages say alliance, not vassalage or homage (the Llywelyn ap Gruffudd page: 'All of the Welsh princes submitted to Llywelyn II except for Maredudd ap Rhys Gryg', without naming Fadog), so the vassal tint is a reading at confidence 1; it keeps the Corwen and Llansilin cells, which Cliopatria's Gwynedd shapes of 1216-1284 contain, from being claimed twice. kingdom-of-gwynedd has no matching vassal event for this state.

ledger.note: 1277: Llywelyn Fychan and Gruffudd Fychan I accept English overlordship and divide the realm. 'In early 1277 an army led by William de Beauchamp, 9th Earl of Warwick' marched into northern Powys; Castell Dinas Bran fell on 10 May and was dismantled; 'under the terms of his surrender the realm would be divided' between Madog II and his brother Llywelyn, and after Madog's death Llywelyn Fychan and Gruffudd Fychan I 'accepted the overlordship of England, and the realm was divided between them'. The page gives no month for the division.

notes: Pages: 2 of 1-2 budgeted (Powys Fadog; Llywelyn the Great, which turned out silent on Fadog). Cliopatria's row is 1169-1215 in two shapes; the page gives 1160-1284 (infobox), so this dossier starts in 1160 (the Powys dossier ends in 1160, leaving 1161-1168 to be covered here with the 1169 shape) and ends in 1284, with new keyframes for 1160-1168 and 1216-1284 that reuse Cliopatria's shapes. OVERLAP: Cliopatria's Kingdom of Gwynedd 1216 shape (and England's 1285 shape) contain all five cells of the 1215 Fadog shape, so the Gwynedd dossier's treatment of 1216-1284 (vassal tint or annexation) must not double-claim them; the pages opened say only 'alliance' (1215, 1258), not vassalage. The 1210 one-cell shrink and the 1216 Gwynedd absorption are undated on the pages. Area: no figure on the page. The commotes named (Maelor, Yale, Nanheudwy, Cynllaith, Glyndyfrdwy, Mochnant Is Rhaeadr) are not gazetteer names (the Wrexham and Denbighshire admin units are); the Cliopatria shape is used instead. Gazetteer names needed: Maelor, Yale (Iâl), Nanheudwy, Cynllaith, Glyndyfrdwy, Mochnant. Not covered by the pages opened: King John and the 1208-1210 events, the 1241-1247 wars, the Treaty of Montgomery's effect on Fadog (1267), the lordships created in 1277 and 1284. The 1160 date is the Powys Fadog page's; the Wenwynwyn page's caption also begins its map at 1160. REPAIR of 2026-10-25 (batch eu-11-i-fixed, after the review): Cliopatria's Fadog shape rasterises to Mold, Holywell, Ruthin and Corwen cells, not to the commotes the page names, so all four keyframes are now 'adjust' with a shape built from the commotes (Maelor 1160; plus Glyndyfrdwy 1169; plus Cynllaith and Mochnant Is Rhaeadr 1210), 2, 3 and 4 gazetteer cells. The Chirk cell is left out (its centre is Oswestry) and the Ruthin cell too (Dyffryn Clwyd). The two growth steps are dated by Cliopatria's shapes only (ledger 1169 and 1210, confidence 1: the page says 'later added' and gives no years), which is why the 1160-1168 core is smaller than the first version's. The capital Castell Dinas Bran now lies in every shape. Added: the 1277 division under English overlordship (Warwick's army, Dinas Bran 10 May 1277) as vassal_start to kingdom-of-england with its 1284 end, and the Gwynedd relation as a vassal tint 1258-1277 at confidence 1 (the pages say 'alliance' and 'forced into an alliance', never homage). Open: Cliopatria's Gwynedd shapes of 1216-1284 contain the Corwen and Llansilin cells; Gwynedd's own ledger draws Tegeingl 1169-1210 and from 1212 (no double claim with the Flintshire cells any more). Pages opened in the repair: Madog ap Gruffydd Maelor, Llywelyn ap Gruffudd (and Powys Fadog again).
